Danish Energy Agency and Energinet (2026). Technology Data - Renewable fuels: Technology descriptions and projections for long-term energy system planning, version number 0015 (latest amendment 08/2026; first published June 2017). ISBN 978-87-94447-50-8. Data sheets: data_sheets_for_renewable_fuels_15 (alldata_long). https://ens.dk/en/analyses-and-statistics/technology-data-renewable-fuels

Workbook Intro sheet: "All cost data is in 2020 EURO, except the chapters on pyrolysis and electrolysis which are in 2025 EURO". Chapters 80 (electrolysis), 86 and 87 (pyrolysis) are therefore 2025_EUR and all other chapters 2020_EUR. Chapter 80 text also says 2025 price level. The report guideline is inconsistent (one line says fixed 2015 prices, another 2020 level); the workbook statement is used.

Scope: chapters 80 (AEC, PEMEC, SOEC at 10 MW/100 MW/1 GW, plus two offshore PEMEC configurations), 81, 83, 86, 87, 89, 91-106 - all 44 data sheets in the workbook. Year loaded: the first data year printed on each sheet (2025 for chapters 80, 86, 87; 2020 for 81, 89, 91, 93, 96, 97, 98, 100; 2015 for 83, 92, 94, 95, 99, 101-106). For HTL (89), 2015 is all n.a., so 2020 was loaded. Lower/Upper are loaded as value-min/value-max only where the catalogue prints them for that same year and as absolute values; for 2015-based sheets the ranges are printed for 2020 only, and for 81 for 2025 only, so they have no min/max in the main file. Several older sheets (89, 92, 93, 95-106 and the technical rows of 98) print uncertainty as multipliers of the central value (e.g. 0.9/1.1, 0.5/1.5, plant size 1/1). These were not turned into min/max; they are listed in _other-values. Later years (and 2050 Lower/Upper) go to _projections.csv with the same transforms. Loaded parameters: description, capacity (MW on the stated basis), annual-output where printed per year, efficiency (main-product output over total input, %, LHV; electrolysers use the HHV-based system efficiency), specific-energy-consumption per input carrier, capex (M EUR/MW x 1000 to EUR/kW; chapter 80 printed in EUR/kW; chapter 91 in k EUR/MW = EUR/kW), opex-fixed (M EUR/MW/yr x 1000, EUR/MWth/yr / 1000, k EUR/MW/yr as is, or % of investment/yr for electrolysers), opex-total where fixed and variable are reported together (81, 86, 87), opex-variable, lifetime, construction-time, load-range-min, degradation-rate (electrolysers, %/1000 h), ch4/n2o/nox factors (94) and methane slip/emission (81, 91). Specific energy consumption: where inputs are printed as MWh/MWh of total input, SEC = input share / main-output share (exact division, formula column, MWh per MWh product, no range). Printed per-tonne inputs (96, 97) are loaded as MWh/t. Electrolysers: system electricity kWh/kg H2 (stack+BOP); SOEC heat = 40 kWh/kg x heat share / electricity share. Flows: co-product outputs (district heat, steam, electricity, glycerine, LPG, naphtha, DDG) per MWh of main product by the same division; CO2, oxygen and water per t product as printed; electrolyser water per t H2 = kg water/MWh / kg H2/MWh. Not loaded (in _other-values): outages (forced/planned; availability cannot be computed exactly from forced-outage % and planned days/weeks), stack replacement interval, stack-level electricity use, LHV-based electrolyser efficiency, cost breakdowns (equipment/installation %, stack/BOP/indirects), per-tonne and per-TPD duplicate cost rows, heat-loss splits, ramp rates and start-up times, footprints and weights, densities and energy contents, CO2 resource, N2 consumption, pyrolysis gas and bio-oil co-products whose commodity is not in the vocabulary, the alternative-configuration rows for slow pyrolysis, and non-numeric entries (-, n.a., <= 5). Chapter 99 (FT from gasification) has no efficiency or SEC: it prints no single main-product share (naphtha, jet and diesel outputs only). COST BASIS: overnight - the guideline defines the investment cost as the EPC price or overnight cost incl. infrastructure and connection costs inside the plant premises; chapter 80 costs include indirects (EPC services). Heating value: the guideline states all energy inputs and outputs are on an LHV basis.

(1) Sheet "80 SOEC 100 MW": from "Hydrogen [kg/MWh input]" to "Frequency of stack replacement" the values are shifted one row (hydrogen 5 kg/MWh, forced outage 14%, planned outage 20 days, lifetime 25,000 years, stack replacement 3.5 h; construction time blank). These rows were not loaded; the water flow was skipped too. (2) Sheet "80 PEMEC 10 MW (Off. cent.)" is titled 10 MW but describes a 100 MW plant (plant size 100 MW input_e). (3) Price year: the guideline text says both "fixed 2015 prices" and "2020-level"; the workbook Intro says 2020 EUR except pyrolysis and electrolysis in 2025 EUR. (4) Several sheets print uncertainty as multipliers rather than absolute bounds, without saying so on the sheet (see extraction-note). (5) 81 biogas: specific investment unit printed as "M EUR/MWh Output" (read as per MW output); "Biogas [%] = 1" is meaningless. (6) 99: specific investment printed as "M EUR/MW Liquids/year" and fixed O&M as "M EUR/MW/year FT Liquids/year"; the naphtha, jet and diesel output shares add up to only 0.25 of total input, which looks low for FT. (7) 100 Jet fuel from hydrogen: plant size printed as "1,000 kt FT Liquids/year" = 2 next to a 3.1 MW plant (read as 1,000 t); fixed O&M printed per MWh of liquids, not per kW-yr. (8) 102: plant size unit printed as "MW biodiesel/year". (9) 106: variable O&M unit printed as "EUR/MW Ethanol" (probably EUR/MWh). (10) 105: ethanol output share is printed as 46 in 2020 (0.46 in 2015 and later years), a unit slip; the 2020 efficiency and the SEC rows derived from it were dropped from _projections. (11) 87 small digestate: fixed+variable O&M central 0.115 lies outside its printed range 0.08-0.1; 87 small straw biochar output central 0.4399 vs range 0.44-0.44 (rounding). (12) 83 and 94 gas output is printed as % of fuel input, while inputs are % of input capacity; the bases are not reconciled. (13) Chapter 80 Lower/Upper labels are not ordered (Lower > Upper for several rows, e.g. heat loss, efficiency upper); min/max were sorted. (14) 91: the auxiliary inputs are per biogas input and the output per methane input; the SEC division assumes these are the same energy.
